chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ibn Bakir, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, for the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) are ten names: five of which are in the Quran and five are not in the Quran. As for those in the Quran: Muhammad (peace be upon him), Ahmad, Abd Allah, Ya Sin, and Nun. And as for those not in the Quran: Al-Fatih, Al-Khatam, Al-Kafi, Al-Muqfi, and Al-Hashir.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten names of the Prophet Muhammad and which ones are found in the Quran?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) delineates the Prophet’s ten names, distinguishing between those explicitly revealed in the Quran (such as Ahmad and Yasin) and those derived from prophetic tradition (like Al-Fatih and Al-Khatim). This classification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the completeness of the Prophet’s identity, linking Quranic titles to divine revelation and extra-Quranic titles to his functional roles in guiding the community.
